aiOverview.content: FISA Section 702 is a controversial U.S. surveillance law allowing warrantless, targeted intelligence gathering on non-Americans located abroad, often sweeping in American communications. Used heavily against foreign espionage and terrorism, its 2026 reauthorization is stalled over privacy concerns, specifically regarding "backdoor searches" of American data by federal agencies.Key Aspects of Section 702Purpose: Authorized under the 2008 FISA Amendments Act, it allows the government to compel U.S. companies (e.g., Google, AT&T) to provide access to communications of targeted foreigners outside the U.S.."Backdoor Searches": While targeting foreigners, the system inevitably captures data on U.S. citizens. Government agencies, including the FBI, have used this to search for American information without a warrant.Controversy & Abuse: The FBI has faced criticism for "widespread violations" of rules, including searching for data on protesters, journalists, and political donors.Reauthorization (2026): Set to expire in April 2026, the law faces intense scrutiny. Opponents demand requiring warrants for accessing U.S. data, while officials argue this would hinder national security efforts, which they claim prevent terrorist acts.The law serves as a major source of foreign intelligence, used for counterterrorism and cybersecurity.Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA): 2026 ...Mar 16, 2026 — The law permits the National Security Agency to acquire the communications of almost any foreigner abroad without obtaining an ind...Brennan Center for JusticeSection 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance ActApr 8, 2026 — Congress will soon vote on the reauthorization of a surveillance authority known as Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Survei...Brennan Center for JusticeU.S. Says Wiretap Program Thwarted Attack on 2024 Taylor Swift ConcertApr 9, 2026 — The court's ruling requires the agencies to re-engineer the filter tools to comply with rules for queries for Americans' informati...The New York TimesWhat is the Fisa law Trump wants extended ... - BBCApr 17, 2026 — "Information collected under the law without a warrant can be used to prosecute and imprison people, even for crimes that have not...BBC
